```json
  "activeInvestigations": []
}
```

This is conceptual.

The registry should not become an unstructured dumping ground.

Its purpose is to answer:

```text
Where is APEX now?
```

### 42.7 State is not history

`APEX_STATE` stores current state.

History belongs in append-only or versioned registries.

For example:

```text
current last-known-good build
```

belongs in state.

All previous builds belong in:

```text
APEX_BUILD_REGISTRY
```

Mixing current state and full history into one structure makes queries and updates error-prone.

### 42.8 Architecture Map

`APEX_ARCHITECTURE_MAP.json` records subsystem ownership.

Conceptually:

```text
AudioEngine
    owns
realtime graph execution

RoutingGraph
    owns
routing topology

RecordingEngine
    owns
capture-to-disk lifecycle

LiveInputMonitorEngine
    owns
wet live monitoring
```

A possible record:

```json
{
  "component": "LiveInputMonitorEngine",
  "authority": "wet-monitoring-contribution",
  "threadRoles": [
    "audio"
  ],
  "relatedFiles": [
    "LiveInputMonitorEngine.h"
  ],
  "invariants": [
    "APEX-AUDIO-MONITOR-001"
  ]
}
```

The map should help the agent answer:

```text
Who owns this responsibility?
```

before creating duplicate logic.

### 42.9 Architecture generation identity

Major architecture migrations should have stable generation IDs.

For example:

```text
ROUTING-GRAPH-V1
ROUTING-GRAPH-V2
ROUTING-GRAPH-V3
```

A fix proven against:

```text
ROUTING-GRAPH-V1
```

may not automatically apply to:

```text
ROUTING-GRAPH-V3
```

Therefore evidence should record architecture generation where relevant.

### 42.10 Capability Registry

`APEX_CAPABILITY_REGISTRY.json` answers:

```text
What can APEX actually do?
```

Recommended states:

```text
NOT_IMPLEMENTED
SCAFFOLDED
EXPERIMENTAL
PARTIAL
PRODUCTION_CANDIDATE
VERIFIED_PRODUCTION
DEPRECATED
```

Example:

```json
{
  "capabilityId": "APEX-CAP-NATIVE-TUNE",
  "name": "Native Tune",
  "status": "EXPERIMENTAL",
  "implemented": [
    "monophonic-pitch-detection"
  ],
  "missing": [
    "formant-preservation",
    "offline-hq"
  ],
  "evidence": [
    "CASE-2026-0042"
  ]
}
```

This prevents:

```text
code exists
```

from being confused with:

```text
feature complete
```

### 42.11 Capability claims require evidence

A capability may not advance to:

```text
VERIFIED_PRODUCTION
```

because:

```text
the UI exists
```

or:

```text
one demo worked
```

It requires defined gates.

For example, Native Tune may require:

```text
realtime safety
latency validation
sample-rate matrix
buffer-size matrix
record/monitor matrix
offline render
save/reload
perceptual validation
```

Capability status must reference its evidence.

### 42.12 Fix Registry

`APEX_FIX_REGISTRY.json` stores verified historical fixes.

Conceptually:

```json
{
  "fixId": "APEX-AUDIO-MONITOR-001",
  "title": "Double Live Input Contribution",
  "status": "VERIFIED_FIXED",
  "rootCause": "Dry and wet monitoring paths both contributed.",
  "invariant": "Exactly one live input monitoring owner.",
  "affectedComponents": [
    "AudioEngine",
    "LiveInputMonitorEngine"
  ],
  "regressionTests": [
    "TEST-MONITOR-MATRIX-001"
  ]
}
```

The registry exists to prevent regression amnesia.

### 42.13 Verified fix versus historical patch

Not every merged patch deserves a Fix Registry entry.

A Fix Registry entry should represent:

```text
meaningful user-visible defect
architectural invariant
serious crash
data-loss issue
realtime defect
important performance regression
```

Minor cosmetic patches may remain ordinary commit history.

The registry should remain high signal.

### 42.14 Invariant extraction

The most valuable part of many fixes is not the code diff.

It is the invariant learned.

Example:

```text
Bug:
double monitoring

Patch:
changed ownership guards

Invariant:
One live input sample has exactly one audible monitoring owner.
```

The invariant survives future refactors better than the patch itself.

Therefore every significant fix should ask:

```text
What rule must never be violated again?
```

### 42.15 Test Registry

`APEX_TEST_REGISTRY.json` records permanent tests and validation procedures.

Each test should identify:

```text
testId
purpose
type
scope
environment
inputs
expected result
related fixes
related capabilities
```

Example:

```json
{
  "testId": "TEST-MONITOR-MATRIX-001",
  "type": "integration",
  "purpose": "Prevent duplicate monitoring contribution",
  "cases": [
    "MonitorDryRecordDry",
    "MonitorWetRecordDry",
    "MonitorWetRecordWet"
  ],
  "protects": [
    "APEX-AUDIO-MONITOR-001"
  ]
}
```

### 42.16 Automated versus manual tests

The registry may contain:

```text
UNIT
INTEGRATION
SYSTEM
PERFORMANCE
SOAK
MANUAL
PERCEPTUAL
```

Manual tests remain valid engineering assets when automation is impractical.

But they must have explicit steps and expected results.

### 42.17 Build Registry

`APEX_BUILD_REGISTRY.json` records build identity.

Conceptually:

```json
{
  "buildId": "BUILD-2026-000119",
  "commit": "abc123",
  "branch": "main",
  "configuration": "x64 Debug",
  "compiler": "MSVC",
  "result": "SUCCESS",
  "warnings": 0,
  "errors": 0,
  "signed": true
}
```

Build identity allows runtime evidence to point to an exact binary lineage.

### 42.18 Last Known Good

The operational state should identify:

```text
LAST_KNOWN_GOOD
```

A build becomes last-known-good only after passing the required gate for its scope.

For example:

```text
build success
```

alone is insufficient.

A release-like last-known-good may require:

```text
build
launch
core smoke tests
recording
playback
export
```

according to current milestone.

### 42.19 Performance Baselines

`APEX_PERFORMANCE_BASELINES.json` may store:

```text
callback p50
callback p95
callback p99
max callback
xrun count
CPU
memory
disk throughput
```

for defined scenarios.

Example scenario:

```text
70-node project
48 kHz
128 samples
specified plugin set
```

Without scenario identity, performance numbers are meaningless.

### 42.20 Performance evidence is environmental

A performance result must include:

```text
CPU
OS
driver
device
sample rate
buffer
build configuration
plugin corpus
```

A measurement from one machine does not automatically prove universal performance.

### 42.21 Evidence directory

Recommended structure:

```text
APEX_EVIDENCE/
    CASE-2026-0001/
        case.json
        baseline.json
        reproduction.md
        trace.json
        crash.json
        build.log
        patch.diff
        tests.json
        verification.json
```

Each case receives a stable ID.

### 42.22 Evidence immutability

Evidence should generally be append-only.

If an earlier conclusion was wrong:

```text
do not silently rewrite history
```

Instead:

```text
supersede
correct
or invalidate
```

with a new record.

This creates an audit trail.

### 42.23 Evidence confidence

A finding may have confidence such as:

```text
LOW
MEDIUM
HIGH
CONFIRMED
```

Example:

```text
Likely data race
```

is not:

```text
Confirmed data race
```

Confidence should be tied to evidence type.

### 42.24 Evidence promotion

A possible lifecycle:

```text
OBSERVATION
    ↓
HYPOTHESIS
    ↓
SUPPORTED
    ↓
CONFIRMED
    ↓
REGRESSION-PROTECTED
```

Not all observations reach the final state.

### 42.25 Machine-readable identity

Every major entity should have stable IDs:

```text
CAP-ID
FIX-ID
TEST-ID
BUILD-ID
CASE-ID
ARCH-ID
```

Human-readable names may change.

Stable IDs should not.

### 42.26 Relationships between registries

The system becomes powerful when registries reference one another.

Conceptually:

```text
CAPABILITY
    ↓
requires
TESTS

FIX
    ↓
protected by
TESTS

TEST
    ↓
executed on
BUILD

BUILD
    ↓
produces
EVIDENCE

EVIDENCE
    ↓
updates
STATE
```

This creates a graph of engineering truth.

### 42.27 No duplicate truth

A critical rule:

```text
One question
→ one canonical authority
```

For example:

```text
current capability status
```

belongs in the Capability Registry.

It should not also be independently maintained in:

```text
README
STATE
FIX REGISTRY
```

Those may reference it.

They should not redefine it.

### 42.28 Repository scanning

An agent may periodically inspect:

```text
files
symbols
modules
tests
build configuration
```

to detect drift.

For example:

```text
Architecture Map says AudioEngine owns X
but the source no longer contains that path.
```

The agent should flag:

```text
ARCHITECTURE MAP STALE
```

rather than silently trusting old memory.

### 42.29 Drift detection

Drift may occur between:

```text
Brain
Architecture Map
Repository
Tests
Runtime
```

Examples:

```text
test references deleted component
fix invariant no longer has test
capability marked verified but tests fail
architecture owner moved
```

A periodic consistency audit should detect these conditions.

### 42.30 Memory invalidation

Operational memory must be invalidatable.

A finding may become stale because:

```text
architecture changed
dependency changed
driver changed
plugin changed
algorithm changed
```

Therefore records may include:

```text
validFrom
validTo
supersededBy
architectureGeneration
```

where appropriate.

### 42.31 Agent query workflow

Before modifying APEX, the agent should query:

```text
1. Architecture Map
2. Capability Registry
3. Fix Registry
4. Test Registry
5. Active State
```

Then inspect the repository.

The registries guide attention.

They never replace source inspection.

### 42.32 Pre-patch memory check

Before patching a subsystem:

```text
search Fix Registry
for related historical defects
```

Example:

```text
editing live monitoring
```

should surface:

```text
APEX-AUDIO-MONITOR-001
```

The agent can then enforce the existing invariant.

### 42.33 Regression collision detection

Suppose a patch modifies:

```text
AudioEngine
```

The memory layer may identify tests protecting that component.

Conceptually:

```text
modified file
    ↓
Architecture Map
    ↓
related invariants
    ↓
related tests
```

This helps select regression tests automatically.

### 42.34 Dependency-aware testing

A local change may affect indirect systems.

Example:

```text
RoutingGraph
```

may affect:

```text
playback
record monitoring
PDC
export
```

The Architecture Map can encode dependency edges.

Then test selection can extend beyond modified files.

### 42.35 Known Regression Registry

Critical unresolved bugs may be stored as active cases.

Possible states:

```text
OPEN
INVESTIGATING
PATCHED
VERIFYING
CLOSED
```

These should not be confused with verified fixes.

### 42.36 Active investigations

`APEX_STATE` may reference:

```text
activeInvestigations
```

so multiple agents do not unknowingly duplicate work.

The record may contain:

```text
caseId
scope
status
lastEvidence
```

### 42.37 Multi-agent coordination

If multiple agents operate on APEX, they should not treat their own local conclusions as globally authoritative.

A shared memory layer may coordinate:

```text
task ownership
active branch
modified subsystem
pending validation
```

Avoid two agents simultaneously redesigning the same authority boundary.

### 42.38 Write permissions

Not every agent should be able to update every registry.

Recommended separation:

```text
read
propose
verify
publish
```

For example:

```text
agent proposes VERIFIED_FIXED
```

but publication may require validation gates.

### 42.39 Registry transaction model

Multiple related updates should commit together.

Example:

```text
Fix Registry
+
Test Registry
+
Evidence
```

should not end in a partial state where:

```text
fix says protected by test
but the test record does not exist.
```

Use transactional publication where practical.

### 42.40 Schema versioning

Every machine-readable registry should contain:

```text
schemaVersion
```

Schema migrations must be explicit.

Agents should not silently reinterpret old fields.

### 42.41 Registry validation

CI or tooling should validate:

```text
unique IDs
valid references
required fields
known enum values
schema version
```

Broken registry references should fail the memory-integrity gate.

### 42.42 Human-readable views

Machine-readable registries may generate:

```text
Markdown dashboards
reports
release notes
```

But generated views are not canonical.

The structured registry remains authority.

### 42.43 State dashboard

A human-facing summary might show:

```text
Current Commit
Last Known Good
Open Critical Bugs
Verified Capabilities
Experimental Capabilities
Recent Fixes
Performance Regressions
```

This can be generated automatically.

### 42.44 Capability maturity

A maturity model may include:

```text
SCAFFOLDED
→ EXPERIMENTAL
→ PARTIAL
→ PRODUCTION_CANDIDATE
→ VERIFIED_PRODUCTION
```

Transitions require evidence.

No manual status promotion without gate references.

### 42.45 Knowledge learned from bugs

A bug can produce four outputs:

```text
Patch
Invariant
Regression Test
Architecture Knowledge
```

The patch solves today.

The other three protect tomorrow.

### 42.46 Example — double-monitoring fix

Observation:

```text
live vocal sounds too loud and distorted
```

Diagnosis:

```text
same input contributes twice
```

Fix:

```text
separate dry and wet owners
```

Invariant:

```text
one audible live-input monitoring owner
```

Regression:

```text
monitoring matrix
```

Memory:

```text
FIX REGISTRY
+
TEST REGISTRY
+
ARCHITECTURE MAP
```

This is the complete knowledge conversion process.

### 42.47 Example — future Native Tune bug

Suppose:

```text
after transport seek,
first vocal note jumps incorrectly
```

The investigation finds:

```text
PitchTrackerCore retained target state
```

The resulting memory may become:

```text
FIX:
APEX-TUNE-TRANSPORT-001

INVARIANT:
Pitch-tracking state must reconcile after transport discontinuity.

TEST:
Seek between unrelated vocal phrases.
```

Future agents automatically see this before modifying tune transport behavior.

### 42.48 Memory aging

Some records become less relevant.

Examples:

```text
old compiler bug
deprecated driver
removed architecture
```

Do not delete important history blindly.

Mark:

```text
SUPERSEDED
ARCHIVED
NO_LONGER_APPLICABLE
```

with reason.

### 42.49 Time-sensitive environment knowledge

Driver behavior or plugin compatibility may be time-sensitive.

Such records require:

```text
verifiedDate
environmentVersion
```

They should not be treated as permanent architecture truths.

### 42.50 Plugin corpus memory

APEX may maintain a validated plugin corpus.

Example fields:

```text
pluginIdentity
format
version
scanStatus
runtimeStatus
sandboxStatus
knownIssues
```

This helps distinguish:

```text
APEX regression
```

from:

```text
known plugin-specific failure
```

### 42.51 Hardware profile registry

Useful hardware profiles may include:

```text
device
driver
sample rates
buffer sizes
known stability
```

Again, these are environment-specific.

Do not generalize one interface result to all devices.

### 42.52 Performance regression detection

A new measurement can be compared against baseline.

Conceptually:

```text
new p99
vs
baseline p99
```

If the regression exceeds project policy:

```text
flag
```

The exact threshold must be defined by APEX release policy.

### 42.53 Automatic test selection

An agent may select tests based on:

```text
modified files
architecture dependencies
historical fixes
capabilities
```

Conceptually:

```text
git diff
    ↓
Architecture Map
    ↓
Affected Capabilities
    ↓
Protected Fixes
    ↓
Required Tests
```

This is one of the strongest benefits of living engineering memory.

### 42.54 Evidence-driven completion

An agent task should end with state update only after evidence exists.

Possible completion outputs:

```text
NO_CHANGE
DIAGNOSED
PATCHED
VALIDATION_PENDING
VALIDATION_FAILED
VERIFIED_FIXED
REGRESSION_FOUND
BLOCKED
SUPERSEDED
```

### 42.55 Memory poisoning risk

A dangerous agent may write incorrect conclusions into shared memory.

Therefore:

```text
memory writes require provenance
```

Every canonical claim should point to:

```text
repository
build
test
trace
or authoritative source
```

Unsupported summaries should not become canonical records.

### 42.56 Contradiction handling

If new evidence contradicts old memory:

```text
do not choose silently
```

Create a contradiction record.

Then:

```text
reproduce
compare environments
resolve
```

The old record may be superseded.

### 42.57 Brain-to-memory promotion

A Brain recommendation may become APEX-specific memory only after implementation evidence.

Example:

```text
Brain recommends immutable snapshots
```

does not create:

```text
APEX uses immutable snapshots everywhere
```

Only repository evidence can establish that.

### 42.58 Memory-to-Brain promotion

The reverse direction also requires discipline.

A bug learned in APEX does not automatically become universal DAW architecture.

It may become:

```text
APEX invariant
```

If the lesson generalizes and is supported by broader evidence, it may later influence the Brain.

### 42.59 Closed learning loop

The complete loop becomes:

```text
EXTERNAL KNOWLEDGE
        ↓
DAW BRAIN
        ↓
APEX DESIGN
        ↓
IMPLEMENTATION
        ↓
BUILD
        ↓
RUNTIME
        ↓
TEST
        ↓
EVIDENCE
        ↓
ENGINEERING MEMORY
        ↓
FUTURE AGENT DECISIONS
```

This is a controlled learning system.

### 42.60 Proposed directory layout

```text
/APEX-INTELLIGENCE
    /schemas
        state.schema.json
        architecture.schema.json
        capability.schema.json
        fix.schema.json
        test.schema.json
        build.schema.json

    APEX_STATE.json
    APEX_ARCHITECTURE_MAP.json
    APEX_CAPABILITY_REGISTRY.json
    APEX_FIX_REGISTRY.json
    APEX_TEST_REGISTRY.json
    APEX_BUILD_REGISTRY.json
    APEX_PERFORMANCE_BASELINES.json

    /evidence
        /CASE-...
```

The exact repository location is a project decision.

### 42.61 Agent startup sequence

On startup, an APEX-aware agent should:

```text
1. Read DAW Brain relevant sections.
2. Read APEX_STATE.
3. Read architecture ownership for task scope.
4. Search historical fixes.
5. Identify required tests.
6. Inspect repository truth.
7. Establish baseline.
```

Only then should it modify production code.

### 42.62 Agent completion sequence

After work:

```text
1. Build.
2. Verify.
3. Run regressions.
4. Write evidence.
5. Update Fix Registry if appropriate.
6. Update Test Registry if new protection exists.
7. Update Capability Registry if maturity changed.
8. Update APEX_STATE.
```

No status should be promoted without evidence.

### 42.63 Ghost-regression detection

A future agent may compare new patches against old invariants.

Example:

```text
Patch adds second monitoring contribution path.
```

Even before runtime:

```text
Architecture Map
+
Fix Registry
```

can flag:

```text
possible violation of APEX-AUDIO-MONITOR-001
```

This is preventative intelligence.

### 42.64 Repository truth refresh

Registries should be refreshed after significant merges.

A stale memory system is worse than no memory if users trust it blindly.

Therefore:

```text
registry freshness
```

must be visible.

### 42.65 Confidence and freshness

A record may expose:

```text
confidence
verifiedDate
commit
architectureGeneration
```

This allows the agent to ask:

```text
Is this still trustworthy for the current code?
```

### 42.66 Security and privacy

Evidence may contain:

```text
paths
usernames
project names
plugin names
audio filenames
```

Support bundles and shared diagnostics should apply privacy rules.

Operational memory should avoid unnecessary personal data.

### 42.67 Backup and recovery

Engineering memory should be version-controlled or transactionally backed up.

Loss of:

```text
Fix Registry
```

would not break the binary.

But it could erase years of engineering knowledge.

Treat it as valuable project infrastructure.

### 42.68 CI integration

CI may enforce:

```text
schema validation
broken-reference detection
duplicate ID detection
required test presence
```

A future advanced gate may also enforce:

```text
critical fix has regression protection
```

### 42.69 Release integration

Before release:

```text
all critical capabilities
```

should have defined maturity.

Open critical regressions should be visible.

The release manifest may reference:

```text
Last Known Good
verified capability snapshot
test evidence
```

### 42.70 Worked example — agent modifies monitoring engine

Task:

```text
Reduce monitoring latency.
```

Agent startup:

```text
reads Architecture Map
```

Finds:

```text
AudioEngine:
dry monitoring owner

LiveInputMonitorEngine:
wet monitoring owner
```

Fix Registry returns:

```text
APEX-AUDIO-MONITOR-001
```

Invariant:

```text
exactly one audible monitoring contribution
```

Test Registry returns:

```text
TEST-MONITOR-MATRIX-001
```

The agent now knows that any latency optimization must preserve this invariant.

After patching:

```text
build passes
```

Then:

```text
monitor matrix runs
```

If double contribution reappears:

```text
patch rejected
```

even if latency improved.

This is engineering memory actively preventing regression.

### 42.71 Worked example — Native Tune maturity

Initial state:

```text
APEX Native Tune:
SCAFFOLDED
```

After pitch telemetry:

```text
EXPERIMENTAL
```

After realtime correction:

```text
PARTIAL
```

After:

```text
realtime safety
monitor integration
offline HQ
save/reload
sample-rate matrix
buffer matrix
```

it may become:

```text
PRODUCTION_CANDIDATE
```

Only after full validation:

```text
VERIFIED_PRODUCTION
```

The Capability Registry makes this progression explicit.

### 42.72 Laboratories

**Laboratory 1 — State registry**
Create an `APEX_STATE` prototype and validate schema.

**Laboratory 2 — Architecture ownership**
Map five APEX subsystems and define their authority.

**Laboratory 3 — Fix conversion**
Take a historical bug and extract:

```text
root cause
invariant
test
```

**Laboratory 4 — Test relationships**
Link one fix to one regression test.

**Laboratory 5 — Last Known Good**
Create a build registry and identify one validated build.

**Laboratory 6 — Drift detection**
Intentionally move a component without updating the Architecture Map and detect staleness.

**Laboratory 7 — Capability maturity**
Create a capability record and define promotion gates.

**Laboratory 8 — Evidence bundle**
Produce a complete case directory for a controlled bug.

**Laboratory 9 — Automatic test selection**
Map a source-file change to required tests.

**Laboratory 10 — Full memory loop**
Execute:

```text
bug
→ diagnosis
→ patch
→ verification
→ fix record
→ test record
→ state update
```

### 42.73 Review questions

1. Why can the Brain not represent current repository truth by itself?
2. What is the difference between current state and historical evidence?
3. Why should architecture ownership be machine-readable?
4. What makes a fix worthy of registry entry?
5. Why is an invariant often more valuable than a patch?
6. How does the Test Registry prevent regressions?
7. Why must performance measurements include environment identity?
8. How can operational memory become stale?
9. What is memory poisoning?
10. Why should unsupported AI conclusions not become canonical memory?
11. What is the difference between Brain-to-memory and memory-to-Brain promotion?
12. How can living memory automatically select regression tests?

### 42.74 Practical examination

Design and implement a prototype operational-memory layer.

The system must include:

```text
State Registry
Architecture Map
Capability Registry
Fix Registry
Test Registry
Build Registry
Evidence directory
```

The student must demonstrate:

```text
stable IDs
schema validation
cross-registry references
one historical fix
one protected invariant
one regression test
one last-known-good build
one capability maturity transition
```

The final demonstration must show an agent querying the memory layer before modifying a protected subsystem.

### 42.75 Mastery rubric

**Foundation**

The learner can explain:

```text
state
capability
fix
test
evidence
```

as different authorities.

**Engineering**

The learner can:

```text
design schemas
maintain stable IDs
validate references
write evidence
```

**Architecture**

The learner can:

```text
map subsystem ownership
design maturity gates
manage invalidation
coordinate tests and fixes
```

**Research**

The learner can:

```text
resolve contradictory evidence
analyze memory confidence
design provenance systems
study long-term regression patterns
```

### 42.76 Permanent APEX living-memory invariants

1. The DAW Brain does not impersonate repository truth.
2. Repository truth is verified from source and runtime.
3. Current state and historical evidence remain separate.
4. Every canonical memory record has stable identity.
5. Important claims include provenance.
6. Unsupported AI conclusions never become canonical Facts.
7. Verified fixes preserve their learned invariant.
8. Critical fixes reference regression protection where practical.
9. Capability status is evidence-gated.
10. Build success does not promote capability maturity automatically.
11. Performance data includes environment identity.
12. Old memory can be invalidated or superseded.
13. Contradictory evidence is resolved explicitly.
14. Architecture ownership has one canonical authority.
15. Registries do not duplicate independent truth.
16. Schema versions are explicit.
17. Broken cross-registry references are defects.
18. Agent memory queries never replace repository inspection.
19. Last Known Good is evidence-backed.
20. Memory writes are auditable.
21. Critical historical regressions remain discoverable.
22. Future agents consult relevant fix history before patching.
23. Engineering memory is backed up and versioned.
24. Privacy-sensitive evidence is minimized.
25. The system can explain why it believes a capability is verified.
26. Living-memory publication never executes on a realtime audio path. Realtime threads emit only bounded evidence according to §34; registry serialization and durable publication follow the non-realtime persistence contracts of §9.
27. Canonical status promotion requires semantic evidence integrity, not merely schema-valid registry syntax.
28. The agent that writes a patch does not acquire verification authority merely by having authored or compiled that patch.
29. A `VERIFIED` status is scoped to its build lineage, architecture generation, validation scope, and available evidence.
30. §§39 and 40 share canonical analysis identity where they operate on the same source material; they do not create competing pitch truths.
31. ARA integration does not become the canonical owner of APEX pitch-analysis or pitch-correction algorithms.
32. Living memory guides repository inspection but never substitutes for it.
33. The DAW Brain claim ledger and the APEX Living Engineering Memory are separate authorities: one audits the document's claims; the other records provenance-bound facts about APEX.

### 42.77 Definition of Done

The Living Repository Intelligence layer is not complete until:

```text
[ ] APEX_STATE schema exists.
[ ] Architecture Map schema exists.
[ ] Capability Registry exists.
[ ] Fix Registry exists.
[ ] Test Registry exists.
[ ] Build Registry exists.
[ ] Performance baseline format exists.
[ ] Evidence case format exists.
[ ] Stable IDs are validated.
[ ] Cross-references are validated.
[ ] Last Known Good is tracked.
[ ] Architecture generations are supported.
[ ] Fix invariants are represented.
[ ] Regression-test relationships exist.
[ ] Capability maturity is evidence-gated.
[ ] Repository drift can be detected.
[ ] Memory staleness is visible.
[ ] Records can be superseded.
[ ] Contradictions can be represented.
[ ] Agent startup queries memory.
[ ] Agent completion writes evidence.
[ ] Automatic test selection is possible.
[ ] Privacy policy exists.
[ ] CI validates memory integrity.
[ ] At least one real historical APEX fix has been migrated into the system.
[ ] Realtime paths never serialize or publish registries.
[ ] VERIFIED states pass semantic provenance gates.
```

### 42.78 Architectural conclusion

The DAW Brain gives APEX long-term technical intelligence.

The Living Repository Intelligence layer gives APEX long-term engineering memory.

Together:

```text
DAW BRAIN
    ↓
what should be understood

APEX REPOSITORY
    ↓
what currently exists

RUNTIME EVIDENCE
    ↓
what actually happened

ENGINEERING MEMORY
    ↓
what has been learned
```

The final system is not merely a document repository.

It becomes a controlled feedback loop:

```text
KNOWLEDGE
    ↓
DESIGN
    ↓
IMPLEMENT
    ↓
MEASURE
    ↓
VERIFY
    ↓
REMEMBER
    ↓
PROTECT
    ↓
IMPROVE
```

This architecture allows future engineers and AI agents to inherit not only APEX's source code, but also the reasoning, invariants, tests, failures, and validated lessons accumulated during its development.

The goal is not to make the agent believe it knows everything.

The goal is to make it impossible for the agent to forget what APEX has already proven.

### 42.79 Primary sources and governing internal sections

Living Repository Intelligence is primarily an APEX architecture recommendation built on existing verified contracts rather than one external standard.

Relevant governing sources and sections include:

- §9 Projects, Files, Undo, and Recovery — stable identity, schema migration, transactional publication, recovery.
- §14 Reference Implementation Blueprint — repository-truth baseline, agent task protocol, Definition of Done.
- §27 Code Signing and Distribution — artifact identity, provenance, manifests, reproducibility, SBOM boundaries.
- §28 DAW Testing and Validation — test taxonomy, regression policy, evidence packages, release gates.
- §31 Recording and Monitoring Architecture — permanent monitoring ownership invariant and regression model.
- §34 RT-Safe Telemetry and Diagnostics — bounded evidence capture, support bundles, crash/trace boundaries.
- §36 Plugin Sandboxing and Crash Isolation — crash/hang/process-failure semantics.
- §41 Autonomous Repository Engineering, Debugging, and Validation Agent — startup, baseline, debugger, patch, validation, and publication workflow.
- [Git documentation](https://git-scm.com/docs/): repository identity and change history.
- [CMake Presets](https://cmake.org/cmake/help/latest/manual/cmake-presets.7.html): reproducible configure/build/test workflow descriptions.
- [SPDX](https://spdx.dev/): software/component and supply-chain information standard family.
- [CycloneDX](https://cyclonedx.org/): BOM and software supply-chain representation.
- [SLSA](https://slsa.dev/spec/): build provenance framework.
